source.scope: All nine printed PFPh ASOP steps and their named clauses, supplemented by shared fire rules and in-volume special procedures. External module/SSR text requires separate verification.

groups: 2.12A · Early SMOKE, IR and MOL Projectors
2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions
2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Remove and disperse existing SMOKE
options.prompt: Which of your old SMOKE counters expire or disperse now?
checks: Remove the owning side’s white Dispersed SMOKE first; then flip its remaining white SMOKE to Dispersed. Do not remove both sides’ SMOKE indiscriminately.
Update dependent drifting counters when the source is removed or reduced. Separate ordinary source cleanup from the special Napalm rule.

Re-evaluate visible LOS and Hindrances before proposing new shots. Link gray drift to its originating source: remove it immediately when that source is removed; when the source disperses, remove the furthest drifting counter under A24.61.
options.effect: Show the affected counters and resulting Hindrance. A considered topic cannot substitute for required cleanup.
options.example: Remove and disperse existing SMOKE / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.11A · Opening cleanup and illumination

options.title: Resolve expiring Napalm Blaze effects
options.prompt: Does removal of Napalm smoke leave burning terrain or destroy equipment?
checks: Identify Napalm-origin smoke and its associated Blaze; generic smoke cleanup loses the information needed here.

On smoke removal, remove the Napalm Blaze in non-Burnable Terrain; in Burnable Terrain make the prescribed Kindling DR to determine conversion to a Terrain Blaze. Resolve the separate 12-FP-column weapon-destruction dr for each eligible SW/Gun, with the pillbox modifier.
Keep this visible for future air-support scenarios even though ordinary Chapter E ground support does not attack in PFPh.
options.effect: Resolve source-linked counters and equipment before continuing.
options.example: Resolve expiring Napalm Blaze effects / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.11A · Opening cleanup and illumination

options.title: Remove due Vehicle Dust
options.prompt: Does this vehicle’s last dust counter expire now?
checks: Check whether the vehicle begins its next friendly PFPh not in Motion, or has been destroyed, stunned, shocked or immobilized as specified.
Do not remove an eligible continuing-Motion dust counter merely because the phase changed; its next MP expenditure can be the removal event.
options.effect: Retain the source vehicle and movement state on each dust record.
options.example: Remove due Vehicle Dust / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.11A · Opening cleanup and illumination

options.title: Attempt opening Starshells
options.prompt: Would illumination help before firing, and which unit should use this hex’s attempt?
checks: Check the initial-use trigger and the one-attempt-per-hex limit. Eligible Good Order non-pinned, non-TI leaders, MMC and CE AFV have distinct Usage thresholds.
After the initial Player Turn of illumination, non-leader Starshell attempts must precede ordinary firing. Leaders retain their later timing exception.
Choose the placement method before its placement dice. Starshell use alone does not consume ordinary fire capability, but hidden/Cloaked firers must be placed concealed.
options.effect: Show one shared hex opportunity, not independent unlimited attempts for every unit in the stack.
options.example: Attempt opening Starshells / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.11A · Opening cleanup and illumination

options.title: Fire ordnance Smoke or WP first
options.prompt: Do you want smoke before any friendly non-SMOKE fire closes the window?
checks: Check ammunition availability, Depletion Number, weather, terrain, range and the appropriate Area Target Type procedure.

SMOKE must precede other friendly non-SMOKE fire. Keep the closure side-wide, not merely a flag on this Gun. Respect the distinct IR and MOL-Projector procedures and ASOP ordering; their early windows do not grant unrestricted later SMOKE fire.
Preview full-strength PFPh placement, WP’s distinct height and morale effects, and ROF rules. An unavailable special-ammo attempt has its own C8.9 accounting.
options.effect: Before committing the first window-closing shot, show unconsidered eligible SMOKE sources without forcing the player to use them.
options.example: AT Gun: smoke screen or HE attack? The checklist shows the shared SMOKE window before the player commits.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.12A · Early SMOKE, IR and MOL Projectors

options.title: Resolve WP checks and possible Flame
options.prompt: Which units and terrain are affected by this WP placement?
checks: Resolve WP NMC using its own terrain/CH rules, not the ordinary HE result path.
Track the source distinction between direct ordnance placement and a WP FFE, which can affect vulnerable occupants throughout its Blast Area.
Resolve any Flame check before moving on. A successful placement is not the end of the action.
options.effect: Create linked resolution rows for each affected disclosed subject and required terrain effect.
options.example: Resolve WP checks and possible Flame / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.12A · Early SMOKE, IR and MOL Projectors

options.title: Fire a mortar Illuminating Round
options.prompt: Is illumination worth giving up this mortar’s other ammunition for the Player Turn?
checks: Confirm IR capability and initial-use permission, then make the Usage dr. Failure is not firing.
On success make the TH DR for malfunction, Low Ammo and SAN purposes; use the IR placement procedure instead of an ordinary target hit.
Firing IR uses all the mortar’s ROF for the Player Turn and prevents another ammunition type. Place No Fire; resolve Gunflash/concealment. Its CA does not change because IR was fired.
options.effect: Distinguish Usage failed, round fired, and failed due to malfunction. Do not offer HE after an IR has been fired.
options.example: Fire a mortar Illuminating Round / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.12A · Early SMOKE, IR and MOL Projectors

options.title: Designate a Spotter for early mortar fire
options.prompt: Does the early mortar shot need a Spotter?
checks: Use eligible Good Order Personnel in the same or adjacent hex; several mortars sharing a Spotter must meet the common-hex and common-target conditions.
Apply spotted-fire TH and ROF penalties. Spotting counts as SW use and restricts movement and inherent fire as specified.
Keep a hidden Spotter private. Replacing a lost original Spotter has a later MPh timing; this is not a free replacement control.
options.effect: Attach the Spotter commitment to the planned early shot and to remaining unit capability.
options.example: Designate a Spotter for early mortar fire / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.12A · Early SMOKE, IR and MOL Projectors

options.title: Fire a MOL Projector before ordinary weapons
options.prompt: Is a MOL Projector attack wanted before non-SMOKE weapons fire?
checks: Predesignate its target and validate range, elevation and CA using C13.5. It is not a squad’s MOL attack.
In PFPh it must precede the first weapon firing other than SMOKE. Leadership does not modify its TH DR.
Resolve its hit, smoke, possible Flame and fire-marker consequences.
options.effect: Display a separate last-chance reminder alongside the SMOKE window.
options.example: Fire a MOL Projector before ordinary weapons / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.12A · Early SMOKE, IR and MOL Projectors

options.title: Gain or maintain artillery contact
options.prompt: Should this Observer commit the phase to the battery?
checks: Validate the Observer, possession, transport/Guard limits and radio or Field Phone. Check nationality/date/PTO modifiers and whether maintenance rather than first contact applies.
Contact/maintenance is the Observer’s sole phase action apart from allowed OBA activities. A failed attempt cannot be retried by this radio or Observer in the same phase.
Distinguish voluntary and involuntary contact loss and their mission effects. Offboard Observers and Creeping Barrages have explicit exceptions, not an assumed radio roll.
options.effect: Compare OBA use with the leader’s competing fire-direction role before commitment.
options.example: Gain or maintain artillery contact / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions

options.title: Request Battery Access
options.prompt: Is Access needed, and does FFE:C make the request mandatory?
checks: Keep Contact and Access separate. Use the battery’s actual draw pile and the required additional-draw conditions.
With Contact and an FFE:C, resolve the mandatory Access attempt and continuation outcome. Do not offer ordinary attacks while an unresolved required branch is pending.
Honor red-card consequences, permanent loss where applicable, and special battery/NOBA rules. Never reveal private draw-pile order.
options.effect: Show the next legal branch after the draw; marking this considered cannot gain Access.
options.example: Request Battery Access / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions

options.title: Choose a new mission and place its AR
options.prompt: Which mission and target are justified by this Observer’s view?
checks: Choose the legal mission type and declare it at the required time. Ordinary HE Concentration, Harassing Fire, SMOKE, IR and Barrage are distinct choices.
Place an AR using Observer LOS and the correct additional-draw tests, then resolve Accuracy and Extent of Error. Do not leak hidden units through legality messages.
A Pre-Registered eligible target may use its direct-FFE procedure. An ordinary SR is not permission to resolve an immediate HE attack.
options.effect: Keep proposed AR, resulting SR and FFE as distinct states, with a visible next decision.
options.example: Choose a new mission and place its AR / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions

options.title: Declare an OBA illumination mission
options.prompt: Should this battery provide illumination instead of a normal fire mission?
checks: Declare IR before the mission’s first Battery Access draw. OBA needs Contact and Access but no mortar-style Usage dr.
Track FFE stage offboard for Access purposes; place IR by its own procedure, not as an FFE Blast Area.
Ordinary IR use consumes the battery’s ROF and other-ammunition opportunity for the Player Turn; apply the separate NOBA exception where authorized.
options.effect: Expose this before drawing, so the interface cannot invite a late retroactive mission choice.
options.example: Declare an OBA illumination mission / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions

options.title: Place a rocket artillery mission
options.prompt: Is this a rocket battery with its own placement and expenditure rules?
checks: Use the rocket AR/FFE procedure and applicable restrictions rather than the ordinary SR correction loop.
Rocket Correction is not allowed. Show the limited mission opportunity and resulting battery state.
options.effect: Do not offer a misleading Correct SR button on a rocket mission.
options.example: Place a rocket artillery mission / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions

options.title: Use an Observation Plane or special Observer
options.prompt: Does this Observer use aerial sighting or shipboard procedures?
checks: For an Observation Plane, resolve applicable Sighting TC and observation restrictions before the battery’s placement and resolution.
Use its actual aerial LOS and mistaken-attack rules rather than ground-Observer visibility.
A Shipboard Observer has its own LOS, accuracy and AR restrictions. Keep offboard and aerial Observer identities distinct.
options.effect: A new Observer profile changes the decision and consequences; it is not just a different icon.
options.example: Use an Observation Plane or special Observer / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.13A · Contact, Access and new artillery missions

options.title: Correct, convert, leave or cancel an existing mission
options.prompt: What does the existing marker and current Observer LOS allow?
checks: Enumerate the alternatives permitted for this exact SR or FFE:1/2 state, including leaving a qualifying SR in place, correction, predesignated conversion, and cancellation.
Require the applicable Contact, Access and Blast-Height/target visibility. Preserve declaration-before-dice ordering.
Do not offer arbitrary backward transitions such as replacing an FFE:1/2 with an SR; apply the special cancellation consequences.
options.effect: Display legal branches with reasons for unavailable ones; pending evaluation remains unknown rather than illegal.
options.example: Correct, convert, leave or cancel an existing mission / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.14A · Existing artillery missions

options.title: Resolve FFE:C continuation
options.prompt: Can the next mission continue here, or must it begin with a new AR?
checks: Resolve the old mission’s cancellation and the permitted new SR/FFE/AR branches after the Access outcome.
Do not treat FFE:C as another attacking FFE.
NOBA forbids the ordinary C1.341/C1.342 continuation shortcuts and requires its new-AR procedure.
options.effect: One continuation decision replaces the old mission; it does not silently extend an HE attack.
options.example: Resolve FFE:C continuation / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.14A · Existing artillery missions

options.title: Correct or lift a Creeping Barrage
options.kind: Scheduled mandatory procedure with specific choices
options.prompt: Which recorded Barrage step is due now?
checks: Use the pre-recorded direction, timing and Lift schedule. Correct/convert and resolve the Creeping Barrage as required; do not ask for normal Observer radio contact.
Distinguish an ordinary Barrage’s geometry from a Creeping Barrage’s compulsory progression.
Represent the allowed early-Lift/conversion decision and later return to ordinary OBA under E12.771, including its delay and Contact/Access requirements.
options.effect: Show the scheduled footprint and mandatory progression, with secret planning visible only to its owner.
options.example: Correct or lift a Creeping Barrage / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.14A · Existing artillery missions

options.title: Place OBA SMOKE or IR before HE FFE
options.prompt: Which smoke or illumination missions must resolve before HE artillery?
checks: Place eligible SMOKE in the actual Blast Area, respecting terrain and weather exclusions and Barrage variations.
Resolve WP NMC and Flame consequences under the FFE-specific rules.
Apply NOBA illumination exceptions through its own mission record; ordinary OBA IR remains distinct from a smoke FFE.
options.effect: Resolve all applicable early effects before HE FFE. Separate placement completion from affected-unit resolution.
options.example: Place OBA SMOKE or IR before HE FFE / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.15A · Artillery resolution and consequences

options.title: Resolve HE FFE and advance its marker
options.prompt: Which hexes and occupants are affected by this mission now?
checks: Resolve the actual Blast Area with the prescribed separate hex DR and all eligible friendly as well as enemy occupants.
Use the applicable protection, level, collateral and special-terrain rules. Do not apply movement-only FFMO/FFNAM in this stationary phase resolution.
Advance FFE:1 to FFE:2 or FFE:2 to FFE:C as required. Involuntary loss of radio contact does not automatically erase all existing FFE effects.
options.effect: The battery stays unresolved until unit and terrain consequences finish.
options.example: Resolve HE FFE and advance its marker / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.15A · Artillery resolution and consequences

options.title: Resolve artillery changes to terrain and fortifications
options.prompt: Did this attack change the map or remove a fortification?
checks: Check the separate conditions for shellholes, Flame, rubble and bridge effects; a qualifying result is not one universal destruction rule.
Check wire, roadblock and pillbox removal, minefield and panji removal/reduction, and sangar or trip-flare elimination.
Include beach-obstacle and pier rules where relevant. Never expose a hidden fortification merely to display a speculative effect.
options.effect: Create per-feature follow-ups with the governing rule and originating attack. This explicitly covers every terrain/fortification family listed in 2.15A.
options.example: Resolve artillery changes to terrain and fortifications / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.15A · Artillery resolution and consequences

options.title: Resolve Column and Reverse Slope effects
options.prompt: Does this artillery resolution break a Column or interact with a Reverse Slope?
checks: Apply Column disbandment when its trigger is met; do not leave its formation state unchanged after the attack.
For NOBA, resolve Reverse Slope protection and exceptions against the naval line of fire, not a generic observer-LOS shortcut.
options.effect: Surface these as dependencies of the actual mission, with pending integration visible.
options.example: Resolve Column and Reverse Slope effects / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.15A · Artillery resolution and consequences

options.title: Mop Up a building
options.prompt: Is securing this building worth committing these units for the turn?
checks: Check armed, unpinned Good Order MMC, the source’s building conditions, no unconcealed unbroken enemy, and coverage of uncontrolled ground-level Locations. Predesignate multiple participants where needed.
One attempt per building per Player Turn. Treat Rowhouses separately and exclude rubble/Blaze Locations as specified. No Quarter/Massacre disables this option.
Reveal hidden units only through the authorized result, remove Dummies, resolve possible casualties and determine Control/surrender only when its conditions are met.
options.effect: Track the building and participants together. In current software, disclose the recorded any-building implementation deviation; final-design eligibility follows the source.
options.example: Two MMC cover a large building together / Both become TI / A hidden defender is revealed concealed, so securing and surrender are not assumed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.21A · Mopping Up, entrenching and Kindling

options.title: Attempt entrenchment
options.who: ATTACKER’s Infantry MMC and participating leader
options.prompt: Would a foxhole improve this position enough to forgo movement and fire?
checks: Check unused eligible participants, terrain, Wire/existing-entrenchment exclusions and special Desert/PTO/beach restrictions. Extreme Winter forbids digging foxholes.
Preview the ordinary final DR of 5 or less, single-HS/crew adjustment, leadership, Labor and applicable nationality/terrain modifiers.
All participants become TI even on failure. Preserve eligible Labor after failure and the actual foxhole capacity/result after success. Entrenching DR can trigger a Sniper.
options.effect: A failed attempt is completed, with Labor and TI tracked separately from success.
options.example: Attempt entrenchment / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.21A · Mopping Up, entrenching and Kindling

options.title: Attempt Kindling
options.prompt: Does the scenario permit deliberate fire here, and is the commitment worthwhile?
checks: Check Burnable Terrain, unpinned Good Order Infantry and the required SMC NTC. Check scenario restrictions on Kindling.
Predesignate all attempts a leader directs in this Location. It cannot wait for one result before adding another unit or simultaneously make its own attempt.
Show terrain Kindling Number, EC, reversed leadership modifier, unit-size and eligible MOL adjustments. All involved use their full Prep Fire capability regardless of outcome.
options.effect: Use Prep Fire consequences rather than incorrectly labeling this as ordinary TI entrenchment.
options.example: Attempt Kindling / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.21A · Mopping Up, entrenching and Kindling

options.title: Choose fire now, Opportunity Fire, or preserve movement
options.prompt: Which units should commit now, and which should retain later options?
checks: Prep Fire normally prevents that unit’s subsequent movement and AFPh fire. Identify linked vehicle/PRC restrictions and exceptions rather than treating every counter independently.
Opportunity Fire defers an eligible Infantry/Cavalry attack to AFPh at full effect but also gives up movement. Simply not firing preserves different choices.
Do not require every unit to fire or every optional topic to be checked. Track individual weapons, SW capacity and leadership commitments.
options.effect: Preview the capabilities given up before execution, then keep retained ROF choices open.
options.example: Squad A fires now. Squad B reserves Opportunity Fire. Squad C holds fire to move. Three deliberate choices, not two incomplete checkboxes.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Fire inherent FP or a fire group
options.prompt: Should these units combine fire or keep separate attacks?
checks: Choose legal target Locations and validate LOS, range and mandatory FG rules before resolving an attack. Group membership is constrained, not any convenient collection of units.
Preview PBF/TPBF, Long Range, Area Fire, concealment, terrain and Hindrances. Keep same-hex and multi-level target rules explicit.
Apply allowed leadership and its direction commitments. Do not suggest splitting an attack where mandatory FG rules require combining it.
options.effect: Show adjusted FP and DRM with provenance, plus the members committed by confirmation.
options.example: Fire inherent FP or a fire group / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Choose Spraying Fire
options.prompt: Would spreading eligible fire across the permitted targets help?
checks: Check the weapon or squad’s Spraying Fire capability, target relationship, range and CA.
Show the halved FP and separate target consequences; do not make this a universal MG or squad option.
options.effect: Keep squad Spraying Fire visible even where the current implementation supports only a narrower attack set.
options.example: Choose Spraying Fire / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification

options.title: Allocate SW and leader direction
options.prompt: Which weapons can this unit use while retaining any inherent fire?
checks: Apply squad/HS/crew/SMC weapon-use limits and the relationship to inherent FP; a SW shot is not free simply because it has a separate counter.
Check captured and non-qualified use, crew-served requirements, ammunition shortage and relevant nationality adjustments.
For MGs include mandatory direction and later ROF direction restrictions. Record the directing leader, not just a numeric bonus.
options.effect: Maintain per-unit capability and per-weapon shots as related records.
options.example: Allocate SW and leader direction / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Choose target type and ammunition
options.prompt: Which legal target type and available ammunition fit this target?
checks: Offer only ammunition and target types provided by the actual weapon notes and scenario/date, while keeping unsupported options readable. Include HE, AP, HEAT, APCR/APDS and special types where present.
Show range, CA, acquisition, size, movement, terrain and qualified-user effects. Resolve hits through IFT or TK as appropriate.
Keep Critical Hits, Multiple Hits, dud/Depletion and malfunction branches distinct. Do not label every miss as an unchanged game state.
options.effect: The attack record captures declared target type/ammo before dice and links resulting effects.
options.example: Choose target type and ammunition / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Consider Canister, IFE and special attack modes
options.refs: C2.29; C8.4; C5.7; C13; weapon notes
options.prompt: Does this weapon have a useful alternative to its ordinary shot?
checks: Represent Canister geometry and ammunition, IFE capability and its fire/ROF accounting, and Deliberate Immobilization eligibility as distinct choices.
For LATW show PF availability, BAZ/PSK/PIAT/ATR restrictions, backblast or Desperation penalties and captured/non-qualified use as applicable.
Weapon and nationality notes select the actual choices and modifiers. Pending IFE or a specific weapon path must not disappear from the guide.
options.effect: Expose modes before commitment and show their separate risk, target restrictions and consequences.

options.title: Designate a mortar’s original Spotter
options.prompt: Does a mortar without an original Spotter need one for this attack?
checks: Designate an eligible original Spotter now, before ordinary mortar fire, using the same capability accounting as early spotting.
Apply +2 spotted-fire TH DRM and reduced ROF where applicable. Pinned Spotter effects propagate to its spotted attacks.
A lost original Spotter cannot be replaced here at will; the source gives replacement timing at the start of the owner’s MPh.
options.effect: Keep early designation, ordinary original designation and later replacement as separate timing windows.
options.example: Designate a mortar’s original Spotter / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Choose vehicle weapons and firing arcs
options.prompt: Which weapons can fire, and what will that do to movement and other weapons?
checks: List MA, SA and individual MGs with crew, exposure, Shock/Stun, Motion and CA eligibility. Do not use one generic fire-tank checkbox.
Apply weapon-combination and turret/hull sequencing rules. A CA change for one attack can change another weapon’s modifiers.

Prep Fire by the vehicle or its PRC has linked movement/fire consequences under D.3; preserve the specific unloading exception for unfired Passengers/Riders. Include LC special armament rules as pending.
options.effect: Compare individual attacks while keeping vehicle-wide commitments visible.
options.example: Choose vehicle weapons and firing arcs / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Use retained Rate of Fire
options.prompt: Did this weapon retain another normal shot, and is it worth taking?
checks: Use the correct colored die and effective ROF after all applicable reductions, including target type, spotting and AA-mode changes.
Re-evaluate target, CA restrictions, leadership and concealment after each resolved shot. Retained ROF is permission for another decision, not automatic firing.
A completed attack must not mark the weapon finished while its legal ROF opportunity remains. Stopping is allowed.
options.effect: Create a new shot opportunity linked to the weapon and current phase, preserving the prior result.
options.example: Use retained Rate of Fire / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Consider Intensive Fire after normal ROF
options.prompt: Is another shot worth the extra malfunction risk?
checks: Require exhausted normal ROF, an eligible Gun, and remaining Intensive Fire capability. Respect No IF weapon notes.
Preview +2 TH DRM and the B# reduction by two under A.11. Do not offer ordinary MG Sustained Fire as a generic Prep Fire extra shot.
Place the correct fire marker and resolve permanent-loss or other weapon consequences as required.
options.effect: Keep IF separate from ROF and explain the risk before rolling.
options.example: Consider Intensive Fire after normal ROF / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Use a flamethrower or squad MOL attack
options.prompt: Does the special weapon justify its range, availability and loss risk?
checks: Check FT eligibility/range and distinguish Personnel/vehicle resolution, relevant protection exceptions, and depletion.
MOL requires its applicable SSR or nationality capability and a successful MOL Check; use its actual inherent-fire and target rules.
Resolve any self-effect, Flame or burning-wreck result. A squad’s MOL is separate from the early MOL Projector timing.
options.effect: Preview risks and possible fire consequences rather than showing only nominal FP.
options.example: Use a flamethrower or squad MOL attack / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Throw a DC or detonate an existing Set DC
options.prompt: Is there a legal thrown or previously Set demolition attack now?
checks: A Thrown DC uses its own range, elevation, attack and thrower-risk procedure; it is not MPh Placement.
A previously Set DC can be detonated in a subsequent Player Turn’s friendly fire phase by its authorized Good Order unit/derivative HS, with the required distance, LOS and NTC.
Resolve malfunction, attack and bridge/rubble consequences. Japanese A-T Set DC keeps its own trigger rules and is not a universal remote detonation.
options.effect: Show who is authorized to trigger the charge and the prior-turn requirement before offering execution.
options.example: Throw a DC or detonate an existing Set DC / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Sequence attacks for Encirclement
options.prompt: Could consecutive attacks establish Encirclement?
checks: Check eligible targets, ranges, directions and firepower under A7.7, including the pillbox and other exclusions.
Qualifying attacks must be consecutive; an intervening attack on a different target can break the sequence.
Keep ordinary and upper-level Encirclement distinct. Do not automatically apply a result just because two units fired at one hex.
options.effect: Warn when a proposed unrelated shot would abandon an identified sequence, without choosing tactics for the player.
options.example: Sequence attacks for Encirclement / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Declare Opportunity Fire
options.prompt: Would firing later at full effect be better than firing or moving now?
checks: Require Good Order and no prior fire/TI this Player Turn. Vehicles cannot use ordinary Opportunity Fire. Place Bounding Fire and apply concealment loss when required.
The unit cannot fire in PFPh or move in MPh. In AFPh it can fire without the usual AFPh penalty and may use permitted ROF/IF.
Infantry-manned ordnance cannot change CA until its AFPh TH attempt. A mortar needs the relevant LOS/Spotter condition; a weapon in AA mode cannot be designated.
options.effect: Show the deferred AFPh opportunity and movement cost immediately, with no target-selection shortcut that bypasses the rule.
options.example: A mortar with a Spotter reserves full-effect AFPh fire. Its CA is not freely changed now, and the reservation remains even if later events spoil the shot.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Use a later Starshell opportunity
options.prompt: Does the current illumination history still permit a Starshell attempt now?
checks: Leaders have the within-phase timing exception. MMC/CE AFV retain later timing only under the initial-illumination conditions.
Use the same per-hex attempt record as the opening window. A failed opening attempt does not create a fresh later attempt.
options.effect: Keep the eligibility explanation tied to scenario illumination history.

options.title: Fire Heavy AA at an aerial target
options.prompt: Does an eligible Heavy AA Gun have a useful aerial target?
checks: Only the qualifying AA Gun without printed IFE uses Heavy AA; this is not ordinary Light AA fire at any convenient time.
Validate aerial targets, including Observation Planes and applicable airborne FAC. Resolve the Heavy AA elimination/damage/prevention outcomes, normal malfunction and ROF.
Update AA mode and its one-attack ROF adjustment as required.
options.effect: Offer an aerial-target workflow with its actual resolution, separate from ground fire.
options.example: Fire Heavy AA at an aerial target / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Assemble or dismantle a weapon
options.prompt: Should the weapon be ready to fire later or easier to carry later?
checks: Validate eligible weapon types and nationality exceptions, possession, and that the weapon has not fired.
Conversion counts as using the SW and all of its ROF; enforce the unit’s weapon-use capacity.
Do not promise that dismantling now allows the possessor to move in this MPh. Show the actual fire/use commitment and resulting PP.
options.effect: Separate conversion success from later fire or movement eligibility.
options.example: Assemble or dismantle a weapon / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Destroy or deliberately malfunction equipment
options.prompt: Would denying this equipment justify losing its use?
checks: The weapon and possessing unit must still otherwise be able to fire it. Count only as many weapons as the unit could use.
Offer destruction and deliberate malfunction as distinct outcomes, each instead of firing. Include vehicular weapons.
Show any resulting vehicle Recall and later repair implications; do not treat permanent destruction as a repairable malfunction.
options.effect: Preview the exact equipment state change before executing, while a reference acknowledgement remains harmless.
options.example: Destroy or deliberately malfunction equipment / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.22A · Fire, Opportunity Fire and weapon handling

options.title: Limber a Gun for later movement
options.prompt: Should this Gun prepare for towing instead of firing?
checks: Check whether the Gun requires/can use limbering, its possession and eligible crew. QSU and NM/RFNM cases are not interchangeable.
Neither Gun nor crew may fire in the Player Turn of (un)limbering. Limbering does not itself make them TI, unlike unlimbering. Show the planned later hookup separately.
Any simultaneous CA adjustment follows the (un)limbering exception, not a free general CA change.
options.effect: Compare fire now with the actual remaining towing sequence; limbering does not itself hook up a vehicle.
options.example: Limber a Gun for later movement / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.23A · Limber and unlimber

options.title: Unlimber a Gun
options.prompt: Is preparing this Gun for future fire worth committing it and the crew now?
checks: Check Gun type, possession, crew and current limbered state.
Apply TI to the Gun and crew as required. Do not offer an immediate normal shot just because the counter is now unlimbered.
Show allowed simultaneous CA selection and the later turn/phase in which the weapon can next act.
options.effect: Track preparation and readiness separately.
options.example: Unlimber a Gun / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.23A · Limber and unlimber

options.title: Change Gun CA without firing
options.prompt: Would repositioning the firing arc now improve a later shot?
checks: Require the crew to remain able to fire the Gun without Intensive/Sustained Fire at phase end, with the explicit exceptions. Retained ROF may preserve this option.
Changing CA here prevents movement of the Gun and crew for the rest of the Player Turn, but does not by itself prevent AFPh fire.
Do not allow an Opportunity-Fire ordnance reservation to evade A7.25’s CA restriction.
options.effect: Show a separate movement commitment without falsely marking an attack as fired.
options.example: An unfired Gun changes CA now, gives up movement, and may fire in AFPh under its actual AFPh restrictions.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path still needs verification
options.timing: 2.31A · Final CA and AA-mode choices

options.title: Designate or cancel AA mode
options.prompt: Should this weapon be prepared for aerial or ground targets?
checks: Use the end-fire-phase CA eligibility criterion even for a weapon that is not a Gun.
Keep AA-capable weapon rules, vehicular AAMG exceptions and Opportunity-Fire incompatibility explicit.
Changing mode by making an attack has different timing and ROF consequences from this end-phase choice.
options.effect: Do not present mode switching as an always-free toggle.
options.example: Designate or cancel AA mode / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: 2.31A · Final CA and AA-mode choices

options.title: Establish or maintain a searchlight beam
options.prompt: Does a searchlight need a new target or a maintenance decision before firing starts?
checks: Apply initial-use triggers and the Starshell-equivalent per-hex attempt rule. Later establishment belongs at the start of friendly PFPh under W10.51.
For an existing beam, choose maintenance with its Reliability DR, or let it cancel and consider a different target. Show malfunction/disablement risk.
A new target uses Sighting TC and the beam’s LOS, CA and illumination rules. Apply the correct fire marker and remaining capability.
options.effect: Place this next to opening illumination in a live checklist, labeled with its Chapter W timing rather than inventing a printed ASOP substep.
options.example: Establish or maintain a searchlight beam / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: Supplemental timing and special rules

options.title: Voluntarily cancel a searchlight beam
options.prompt: Would cancelling the beam change visibility or exposure usefully?
checks: Cancellation is available during the owner’s PFPh under its rule, and at other times only under the separately specified conditions.
Remove the beam and update applicable Gunflash/illumination effects. This is not repairing or re-aiming the light.
options.effect: Recompute disclosed visibility without counting cancellation as a new Sighting attempt.
options.example: Voluntarily cancel a searchlight beam / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.
options.timing: Supplemental timing and special rules

options.title: Conduct Korean War Close Air Support
options.prompt: Does a qualifying FAC-directed aircraft have a legal PFPh attack?
checks: Use the Chapter W exception immediately after all FFE. Ordinary Chapter E air support is not thereby granted PFPh attacks.
Require FAC/TACP direction and its Contact, LOS and target limitations. An aircraft cannot conduct Ground Support in two consecutive Player Turns.
Expose DEFENDER Light AA, mistaken-attack handling and immunity zones. Resolve the source-specific Residual FP and other consequences.
options.effect: This creates a real defender response window inside Prep Fire, despite ordinary Prep Fire attacks belonging to ATTACKER.
options.example: Conduct Korean War Close Air Support / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Apply Naval OBA mission exceptions
options.prompt: Does this naval mission differ from ordinary OBA?
checks: Apply SFCP/Observer, Access, Blast Area, naval line-of-fire and Reverse Slope rules to the corresponding mission steps.
Keep the FFE:C new-AR requirement visible.
A qualifying NOBA battery of at least 150mm can fire IR with its HE/WP mission under G14.672, using its placement restriction. Do not apply the ordinary OBA IR prohibition without this exception.
options.effect: Attach this profile to the individual battery; do not provide disconnected generic naval buttons.
options.example: Apply Naval OBA mission exceptions / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Apply nationality, terrain and equipment restrictions
options.refs: A19; A21; A25; G.3; G11.8; G12.5; W7.41; Chapter H notes
options.prompt: Which specific rule changes this unit’s permitted attack?
checks: Check nationality, elite status, captured/non-qualified use, ammunition shortage and the weapon’s listing/date/notes. Make unsupported configurations visible with unknown eligibility.
Include PTO multi-hex FG restrictions, cave firing/SMOKE and LC armament conditions.
Qualifying Good Order CPVA squad/HS attacks at non-ADJACENT targets in PFPh or using Opportunity Fire are Area Fire unless directed by a leader under W7.41. Preserve the Recon Unit exception.
options.effect: Modifiers must attach to the proposed shot. Chapter H equipment entries and scenario SSR are source profiles, not a claim that every weapon uses one generic rule.

options.title: Resolve the prisoner-elimination rule
options.prompt: Does A20.4 apply in this Location?
checks: Show the exact nationality/status and no-Melee restrictions. The optional action counts as SW use.
The berserk-unit-with-prisoners case has a compulsory start-of-fire-phase result and loss of berserk status; it is an exception to the usual no-Prep-Fire guidance for berserk units.
Apply No Quarter/Mopping Up restrictions and the once-only enemy ELR increase as specified.
options.effect: Use the rule’s neutral description and consequences; neither hide the option nor suggest it as a tactic.
options.example: Resolve the prisoner-elimination rule / Review subject and scenario / Pending rules remain visible; no game action is performed.

options.title: Consider standing choices and ongoing commitments
options.prompt: Will this action affect an ongoing obligation or standing choice?
checks: Retain voluntary concealment loss and automatic Guard Deployment where their own rules permit them. Do not turn prisoner transfer into a PFPh choice.
Apply voluntary/mandatory WA changes at their legal windows, never retroactively after an attack is declared to improve its defense.
Firing can interrupt replenishment. Using an Ammo Vehicle’s Prep Fire benefit restricts that vehicle’s subsequent movement; show the linked commitment.
options.effect: Cross-phase records persist into Prep Fire and update when an actual event changes them.

options.title: Resolve attack results before the next decision
options.prompt: Which required results remain from this shot?
checks: Resolve random selection, casualties, MC/PTC, wounds, leader-loss effects and applicable HOB or special morale changes in their proper sequence.
Resolve collateral effects, Shock/Stun/Recall, burning wrecks, equipment destruction, Cowering, malfunction and ammunition depletion where triggered.
Update concealment, Control/WA and capability only from authorized results. Never mark the attack finished while a dependent choice remains.
options.effect: Separate attacker choices from defender resolution, keep private information private, and reopen only newly created opportunities.

options.title: Resolve Sniper attacks and checks
options.prompt: Did a qualifying Original DR activate a Sniper?
checks: PFPh is Sniper-capable. Check qualifying TH, MC, TC, non-OBA IFT and Entrenching DR, with the Prisoner and other exclusions. Do not treat every DR or dr as a trigger.
Finish the triggering roll’s required effects before the Sniper attack, and respect chained-result ordering. Offer the permitted Sniper Check when its conditions arise.
Include night, LC/seaborne exceptions. ASOP references RB CG8, ABtF CG8, BRT CG8, KGP CG16 and PB CG13; their complete module text needs its own source profile.
options.effect: The response can change later eligibility, so rerun affected opportunities after resolution.

options.title: Resolve a triggered Field Phone cut
options.prompt: Did an opposing unit’s Original 2 trigger a phone-security consequence?
checks: Check the specified security-area and opposing-unit conditions for an Original 2 DR for any purpose.
Keep phone information private, and distinguish a cut/non-repairable phone from a malfunctioned repairable radio.
options.effect: Link this to the triggering roll, rather than inserting a voluntary phone-cutting action.

options.title: Keep later-phase actions in their proper windows
options.prompt: Are you looking for something that belongs to another phase?
checks: Normal SW Recovery/Transfer/repair are not generic Prep Fire actions. MPh smoke grenades, vehicle smoke dispensers and placed DC keep their own windows.
Clearance declarations, Gun hookup/unhooking and Pushing normally belong in MPh; entrenching, Mopping Up and Kindling have the PFPh windows described here.
Defensive First Fire, ordinary Fire Lanes, Subsequent First Fire and FPF are not ordinary Prep Fire attacks. Ordinary air Ground Support has its own timing; the Chapter W CAS exception is separate.
Do not remove Prep Fire, Bounding Fire or TI simply because PFPh ends; use their actual later removal rules.
options.effect: Offer a future-phase reminder, not an invalid action button.

glossary.SMOKE: The umbrella for Smoke and WP effects; preserve ammunition type, owner and source.
glossary.WP: White Phosphorus, with its own height, NMC and ignition rules.
glossary.PFPh: Prep Fire Phase, the ATTACKER’s early fire and preparation window.
glossary.Blaze: A continuing fire state, distinct from a Flame and from its smoke counter.
glossary.SW: Support Weapon. Using one affects its possessor’s capability accounting.
glossary.Motion: Vehicle state. It changes firing eligibility and Vehicle Dust timing.
glossary.LOS: Line of Sight. Guidance uses only information the viewing player may know.
glossary.IR: Illuminating Round, with its own usage and placement procedure.
glossary.dr: One die, distinct from a two-dice DR.
glossary.MMC: Multi-Man Counter: squad, half-squad or crew.
glossary.SMC: Single-Man Counter, such as a leader or Hero.
glossary.TH: To Hit roll or number for an ordnance attack.
glossary.ROF: Rate of Fire. A retained opportunity is not an automatic shot.
glossary.s#: Smoke Depletion Number on the actual weapon. Distinguish s from WP availability.
glossary.DR: Two-dice roll. Keep Original, modified and individual colored/white values.
glossary.SAN: Sniper Activation Number, tested only for qualifying Original rolls.
glossary.MOL: Molotov Cocktail. A squad MOL and a MOL Projector have different procedures.
glossary.Radio Contact: Communication state, separate from Battery Access.
glossary.FFE: Fire For Effect. FFE:1, FFE:2 and FFE:C have different actions.
glossary.Battery Access: Permission to use the battery, determined by its access procedure.
glossary.FFE:C: Continuation marker; it is not an attacking FFE.
glossary.AR: Artillery Request marker, placed before Accuracy resolution.
glossary.Harassing Fire: OBA mission with different area and firepower from a Concentration.
glossary.Barrage: An artillery pattern; a Creeping Barrage additionally follows recorded progression.
glossary.PRC: Passengers, Riders and Crew, with different vulnerability and fire restrictions.
glossary.Column: A formation with specific disbandment rules.
glossary.TI: Task Involved status, not a synonym for Prep Fire.
glossary.HIP: Hidden Initial Placement. No guide prompt may leak hidden opposing information.
glossary.Control: Rules-defined ownership of Locations or buildings, not simply current occupancy.
glossary.DRM: Modifier to a two-dice roll. A drm modifies a single die.
glossary.Labor: Progress modifier/status from eligible unsuccessful labor attempts.
glossary.MPh: Movement Phase. Several Prep Fire commitments prevent subsequent movement.
glossary.AFPh: Advancing Fire Phase. Opportunity Fire reserves a full-effect attack here.
glossary.FG: Fire Group, subject to formation and mandatory grouping rules.
glossary.TK: To Kill resolution, distinct from the To Hit roll.
glossary.IFE: Infantry Firepower Equivalent, a weapon-specific alternative to ordinary TH fire.
glossary.C: Canister ammunition, in this ordnance context.
glossary.IF: Intensive Fire, an extra Gun shot with accuracy and malfunction penalties.
glossary.B#: Breakdown Number, with relevant reductions applied under the actual rule.
glossary.US#: Unit Size Number, used in the Set DC procedure.
glossary.Encircled: State established by qualifying fire or other specific rules.
glossary.FAC: Forward Air Controller in the applicable Chapter W rules.
glossary.dm: Dismantled weapon state, distinct from DM.
glossary.Gun: Rules-defined ordnance, not every weapon colloquially called a gun.
glossary.QSU: Quick Set Up, affecting Gun handling.
glossary.SL: Searchlight in this Chapter W context; not the Squad Leader game abbreviation.
glossary.IB Lane: Illuminating Beam Lane created by a searchlight.
glossary.Gunflash: Night firing signature, governed by its own placement/removal rules.
glossary.Residual FP: Firepower left for qualifying later movement attacks; not an ordinary Prep Fire byproduct.
glossary.SFCP: Shore Fire Control Party for NOBA.
glossary.SSR: Scenario Special Rule. Unknown content is a source gap, not assumed inapplicable.
glossary.Berserk: Special morale state; ordinary Prep Fire is prohibited, with specific rule exceptions.
glossary.Ammo Vehicle: Ammunition-supply vehicle with linked firing and replenishment commitments.
glossary.K: Casualty Reduction result, distinct from KIA.
glossary.HOB: Heat of Battle, a triggered resolution rather than an optional action.
glossary.DM: Desperation Morale, distinct from dismantled dm.
glossary.DFPh: Defensive Fire Phase, distinct from defensive responses during Prep Fire.
